*This page is a benchmark of the method. To use repdist on your own data, start with [Get started](vignette.html).*

In plain terms: one simulated contrast is scored with MMD and with the
alternatives that also use protein similarity, optimal transport and
UniFrac, rather than with Bray-Curtis.

Group A's ten samples each enrich a different domain of one CATH FunFam;
group B's each enrich a different domain of a second FunFam. Three sample
distances built on the same TM-Vec similarity matrix, and optimal transport
on the MCL graph for comparison, are compared on the same counts.

```{r libs}
library(repdist)
library(ggplot2)
library(vegan)
n_cores <- BiocParallel::multicoreWorkers()
```

# Simulation

The FunFam domain universe and the negative-binomial count model of
[Simulation 1](simulation_funfam.html): every domain is present at a
log-normal baseline in every sample, and each sample puts $\rho$ = 2% of its
expected abundance on its enriched domain. The $k$-th enriched domain of
group B takes the baseline abundance of the $k$-th of group A. The two
FunFams are drawn with a fixed seed from those with at least ten domains.

**Data.** The input file is [`curated/simulation_funfam.rds`](https://github.com/Yixuan39/repdist/raw/gh-pages/curated/simulation_funfam.rds) (1.1 MB), in the repository's [`curated/`](https://github.com/Yixuan39/repdist/tree/gh-pages/curated) folder on the `gh-pages` branch, built by `data-raw/simulation_funfam.R`. To run the code on this page, save it in a `curated/` folder next to your working directory.

```{r simulate}
ff <- readRDS(file.path("curated", "simulation_funfam.rds"))
ann <- ff$annotation
stopifnot(identical(ann$domain, names(ff$proteins)))
nb_counts <- function(up, ids, rho, pairs, depth = 2e4) {
    n <- length(up)
    pi <- setNames(rlnorm(length(ids)), ids)
    pi[pairs[, 2]] <- pi[pairs[, 1]] # matched baseline of enriched domains
    pi <- pi / sum(pi)
    s <- rlnorm(n, 0, 0.25)
    e <- rlnorm(length(ids), 0, 0.5)
    p <- matrix((1 - rho) * pi, n, length(ids), byrow = TRUE,
        dimnames = list(names(up), ids))
    for (j in seq_len(n)) {
        p[j, up[[j]]] <- p[j, up[[j]]] + rho / length(up[[j]])
    }
    mu <- s * depth * p
    phi <- (0.1 + 1 / mu) * rep(e, each = n)
    matrix(rnbinom(length(mu), mu = mu, size = 1 / phi), n,
        dimnames = dimnames(p))
}
n_per_group <- 10L
size <- table(ann$family)
set.seed(20261009)
fams <- sample(names(size)[size >= n_per_group], 2)
ff$families[match(fams, ff$families$family), c("family", "name")]
pairs <- vapply(fams, function(f) {
    sample(ann$domain[ann$family == f], n_per_group)
}, character(n_per_group))
up <- as.list(c(pairs))
names(up) <- sprintf("s%02d", seq_along(up))
counts <- nb_counts(up, ann$domain, 0.02, pairs)
group <- factor(rep(c("A", "B"), each = n_per_group))
```

# Distances

On unit-norm TM-Vec embeddings the cosine similarity is the predicted
TM-score $\widehat{TM}$. MMD, OT (TM) and weighted UniFrac use the
domain-by-domain matrix $1 - \widehat{TM}$, with no similarity gate and no
MCL bins.

- **MMD**: `sample_mmd()`, the maximum mean discrepancy under a Gaussian
  kernel on the embeddings, $\exp(-(1 - \widehat{TM}) / \sigma^2)$
  [@gretton2012mmd].
- **OT (TM)**: optimal transport, the exact 1-Wasserstein distance between the
  samples' relative abundances with cost $1 - \widehat{TM}$
  [@peyre2019cot], solved by `transport::wasserstein()`
  [@schuhmacher2024transport]. $1 - \widehat{TM}$ is not a metric, so each
  pair is solved on the full support.
- **OT (MCL graph)**: the same, with the cost read from the weighted graph
  that MCL clusters (`protein_similarity()`, package defaults). An edge
  costs $1 - \widehat{TM}$, two domains cost their shortest path, and
  domains with no path, or a path longer than 1, cost 1. With no edges every
  pair costs 1 and this is Bray-Curtis on relative abundances.
- **Weighted UniFrac**: the domains are joined by average linkage (UPGMA)
  on $1 - \widehat{TM}$, and weighted UniFrac [@lozupone2007unifrac] is
  computed on the domain counts with `GUniFrac` [@chen2012gunifrac]. It is
  the 1-Wasserstein distance under the tree's path metric [@evans2012kr],
  so it differs from OT only in replacing $1 - \widehat{TM}$ by its
  UPGMA tree.

```{r distances}
Z <- S4Vectors::mcols(ff$proteins)$embedding
Z <- Z / sqrt(rowSums(Z^2))
rownames(Z) <- names(ff$proteins)
C <- pmax(1 - tcrossprod(Z), 0) # 1 - predicted TM
diag(C) <- 0
tree <- ape::as.phylo(hclust(as.dist(C), "average"))
# similarity graph (predicted TM >= 0.7, half of both aligned) for OT (MCL graph)
S <- protein_similarity(ff$proteins, n_cores = n_cores)
edges <- which(upper.tri(S) & S > 0, arr.ind = TRUE)
graph <- igraph::graph_from_data_frame(data.frame(rownames(S)[edges[, 1]],
    rownames(S)[edges[, 2]]), directed = FALSE, vertices = rownames(S))
C_graph <- pmin(igraph::distances(graph, weights = 1 - S[edges]), 1)
stopifnot(identical(rownames(C), colnames(counts)),
    identical(rownames(C_graph), colnames(counts)))
ot <- function(p, C) {
    ij <- combn(nrow(p), 2)
    OT <- matrix(0, nrow(p), nrow(p), dimnames = list(rownames(p),
        rownames(p)))
    # forking is safe for transport; sample_mmd() stays serial
    OT[t(ij[2:1, ])] <- unlist(parallel::mclapply(seq_len(ncol(ij)),
        function(k) {
            transport::wasserstein(p[ij[1, k], ], p[ij[2, k], ], costm = C,
                p = 1)
        }, mc.cores = n_cores))
    as.dist(OT)
}
distances <- function(counts) {
    p <- counts / rowSums(counts)
    list(
        MMD = sample_mmd(counts, ff$proteins), # embedding distance
        `OT (TM)` = ot(p, C),
        `OT (MCL graph)` = ot(p, C_graph),
        `weighted UniFrac` = as.dist(GUniFrac::GUniFrac(counts, tree,
            alpha = 1, verbose = FALSE)$unifracs[, , "d_1"])
    )
}
D <- distances(counts)
```

```{r checks, include = FALSE}
# weighted UniFrac = W1 under the tree's path metric / (2 x tree height);
# the path metric is a metric, so only (p - q)+ against (p - q)- moves
p <- counts / rowSums(counts)
path <- ape::cophenetic.phylo(tree)[colnames(p), colnames(p)]
H <- max(ape::node.depth.edgelength(tree))
d <- p[1, ] - p[2, ]
stopifnot(all.equal(as.matrix(D$`weighted UniFrac`)[2, 1],
    sum(d[d > 0]) * transport::wasserstein(d[d > 0] / sum(d[d > 0]),
        -d[d < 0] / sum(-d[d < 0]), costm = path[d > 0, d < 0], p = 1) /
        (2 * H)))
```

# PCoA

Ellipses are 95% ellipses per group (multivariate t).

```{r pcoa, echo = FALSE, fig.width = 8.5, fig.height = 7.5, fig.alt = "PCoA of the simulated FunFam contrast under MMD, optimal transport on the TM-Vec predicted TM-score and on the MCL graph, and weighted UniFrac, coloured by group, with 95% ellipses"}
ord <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(D), function(m) {
    e <- cmdscale(D[[m]], k = 2, eig = TRUE)
    rel <- 100 * e$eig / sum(e$eig[e$eig > 0])
    data.frame(PCo1 = e$points[, 1], PCo2 = e$points[, 2], group = group,
        panel = sprintf("%s\nPCo1 %.0f%%, PCo2 %.0f%%", m, rel[1], rel[2]))
}))
ord$panel <- factor(ord$panel, unique(ord$panel))
ggplot(ord, aes(PCo1, PCo2, colour = group)) +
    geom_point(size = 2) +
    stat_ellipse(linewidth = 0.4) +
    facet_wrap(~panel, scales = "free", nrow = 2) +
    labs(colour = NULL) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

# PERMANOVA

`adonis2()`, 999 permutations [@anderson2001permanova; @oksanen2025vegan].

```{r permanova}
permanova <- function(D) {
    t(vapply(D, function(d) {
        set.seed(1)
        a <- adonis2(d ~ group, data = data.frame(group = group),
            permutations = 999)
        c(R2 = a$R2[1], F = a$F[1], p = a$`Pr(>F)`[1])
    }, numeric(3)))
}
knitr::kable(permanova(D), digits = 3)
```

# Replicates

The contrast above is one draw. It is repeated 50 times at $\rho$ = 0%, 1%
and 2%, with the same two FunFams; each replicate redraws the enriched
domains, the baseline and the counts, and uses the same seed at every
$\rho$. At $\rho$ = 0% the groups differ only in label, so the samples are
exchangeable and every distance should give an R^2^ averaging
$1 / (n - 1)$ = `r round(1 / (2 * n_per_group - 1), 3)` and reject at
p < 0.05 in about 5% of replicates.

```{r replicates}
grid <- expand.grid(replicate = seq_len(50), rho = c(0, 0.01, 0.02))
rep_res <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(grid)), function(r) {
    set.seed(grid$replicate[r])
    pairs <- vapply(fams, function(f) {
        sample(ann$domain[ann$family == f], n_per_group)
    }, character(n_per_group))
    up <- as.list(c(pairs))
    names(up) <- sprintf("s%02d", seq_along(up))
    a <- permanova(distances(nb_counts(up, ann$domain, grid$rho[r], pairs)))
    data.frame(grid[r, ], method = rownames(a), a, row.names = NULL)
}))
rep_res$method <- factor(rep_res$method, names(D))
tab <- do.call(cbind, lapply(split(rep_res, rep_res$rho), function(x) {
    q <- tapply(x$R2, x$method, quantile, c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75))
    cbind(R2 = vapply(q, function(v) {
        sprintf("%.3f (%.3f-%.3f)", v[2], v[1], v[3])
    }, ""), `p < 0.05` = sprintf("%.0f%%",
        100 * tapply(x$p < 0.05, x$method, mean)))
}))
colnames(tab) <- paste0(colnames(tab), ", rho ",
    rep(c("0%", "1%", "2%"), each = 2))
knitr::kable(tab, caption = paste("PERMANOVA over 50 replicates per rho:",
    "median R2 (interquartile range) and the share of replicates with",
    "p < 0.05."))
```
